cells.tense: You are in the middle of that crossing right now, and your footing is actually good.
cells.ask: Take one small step on something unresolved — one email, one draft, one call — and let it stay small today.
cells.core:
You are walking across something that matters, and you are not rushing it. You can hold the not-knowing long enough to take the next step, and the next one shows up when you get there. Most people force the whole thing into view before they move, and you are not doing that.

What is working is that you are reading the ground as you go. You do not need the full picture before you trust your feet, and it is revealing itself because you are actually on it. Keep walking at this pace. What this balance is free to feed next is the part of you that can go first for other people — not by showing them the way, but by being visibly on it.

cells.tense: You are trying to finish the crossing before you are even halfway across it.
cells.ask: Pick the one part of this that is yours to carry, and leave the rest on the ground for now — physically set it down.
cells.core:
You can feel the far side already, so you are walking toward it faster than your feet can go. A conversation becomes a way to settle what is still open, and you push toward a shore that has not been reached yet. The pressure is not moving you across. It is making the crossing longer.

What you want on the other side is being able to pass something on without forcing it, belonging without having to hold it all together. That comes when the bracing drops and the unknown is just the ground you are standing in. The whole way does not have to be visible. You can stop building it ahead of yourself and walk what is under your feet.

cells.tense: You turned back at a crossing you already started, and you are still standing at the old edge.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you actually know about what connects people here — one clear observation — and say it to someone this week.
cells.core:
You stopped in the middle of a passage. The way did not close; you just stopped moving on it. Now you wait for the crossing to feel clear before you take it, and since it does not feel clear, you stay on the near side. The part of you that can move through uncertainty is not broken. It just has no fuel right now.

What is missing here is a pattern you can trust — something you have seen enough times to know it is real. Notice one thing about how people actually connect, say it out loud, and let that be the next step. The old edge has kept you safe and it has kept you still. You do not have to cross today. You just have to take one step that is not backward.

cells.tense: You are already navigating something with real skill, and you are calling it just getting through.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made recently to move through something unclear, and say out loud: that was your call.
cells.core:
You are moving through ambiguity right now — not forcing clarity, not freezing, just walking with what light you have. You do it well enough that it looks like nothing. But it shapes how you talk to people, what you share, what you let stay unanswered. That is real navigation, and it is yours.

What is not happening is you claiming it. You describe the crossing as something that happened to you, not as something you are steering through. The quiet skill does work that gets no credit — and the one person who could give it has not. Say what you are actually doing out loud. Not the whole road. Just the part already walked.
